facts.problem: A person-property override can prevent a same-named group property from being loaded.
facts.trigger: For example, when the request supplies a person property named `tier`, `flags_require_db_preparation` treats that as satisfying an organization filter also named `tier`, even though matching reads those values from separate property maps.
mechanism: The flag is therefore excluded from database preparation.
During matching, the organization's `tier` is still unfetched, so the new fail-closed check returns false.
facts.result: This makes both `organization.tier == "enterprise"` and `organization.tier != "enterprise"` return false regardless of the organization's stored value.
facts.requested_change: Please make `PropertyFilter::requires_db_property` distinguish person and group filters, so person overrides satisfy only person filters.
facts.regression_case: Add a request-level regression test where the person and organization both have a `tier` property.

bad_description:
`blocking`: This collector never sees a mixed-targeting flag when a same-named person override makes its explicit group filter look satisfied. `prepare_evaluation_state_if_needed` passes only person overrides to `flags_require_db_preparation`, and `PropertyFilter::requires_db_property` ignores the filter type. For example, a person-aggregated condition on `organization.tier` is skipped during DB preparation when the request also supplies a person property named `tier`. The group remains pending, so both positive matches and valid negative matches return false even when the stored organization satisfies the filter.

Make explicit group filters require group DB preparation independently of person overrides, then add a request-level regression case with a person-aggregated condition, an explicit group index, and a same-named person override.
desired_description:
`blocking`: A person-property override can prevent a same-named group property from being loaded. For example, when the request supplies a person property named `tier`, `flags_require_db_preparation` treats that as satisfying an organization filter also named `tier`, even though matching reads those values from separate property maps.

The flag is therefore excluded from database preparation. During matching, the organization's `tier` is still unfetched, so the new fail-closed check returns false. This makes both `organization.tier == "enterprise"` and `organization.tier != "enterprise"` return false regardless of the organization's stored value.

Please make `PropertyFilter::requires_db_property` distinguish person and group filters, so person overrides satisfy only person filters. Add a request-level regression test where the person and organization both have a `tier` property.
mechanisms_without_explanation: `blocking`: `prepare_evaluation_state_if_needed` passes only person overrides to `flags_require_db_preparation`, and `PropertyFilter::requires_db_property` ignores the filter type. The group remains pending, so positive and negative matches return false. Make `requires_db_property` distinguish filters and add request coverage.
consequence_last: `blocking`: `prepare_evaluation_state_if_needed` passes the person overrides to `flags_require_db_preparation`. The matching path then leaves the organization pending and the fail-closed check returns false. Make `PropertyFilter::requires_db_property` distinguish person and group filters and add request coverage, because otherwise both equality and inequality checks ignore the organization's stored value.
already_clear:
`blocking`: A request without an email reaches `validate_user` with `email` set to `None`. The function calls `.lower()` on that value, which raises `AttributeError` and returns a 500.

Check for `None` before normalizing the address, and add a request test without an email.
